title: [D9 Research] Evaluation corpus requirements and provider quota sizing
summary: `docs/evaluation-corpus.md` is now the written requirement for the corpus the whole project's measurements are gated on: the labelling scheme (context granularity, `context_version`, `helena.taxonomy.v1`'s vocabulary, `unknown` as a label and not a gap, entity-level truth beside context-level truth, labeller provenance and a measured agreement rate), host and time coverage, episode identifiers and a marked decisive window for multi-stage activity, time correctness, the quota ceiling, the base-rate hazard, the retrieval confound, and each of `concept/01`'s eight research questions with its measurement and its blocker. `scripts/corpus_sizing.py` (`make corpus-sizing`) computes the ceiling from `config/policy.toml` rather than from a number in a document, and `tests/test_evaluation_corpus.py` recomputes every table in the document on every run and parses the two concept notes the document depends on. The evaluation harness is untouched and still deferred.
assumption_validated: That the corpus requirement can be made *falsifiable* rather than aspirational — expressed against identifiers, vocabularies and budgets the pipeline already has, with the quota arithmetic executable. It can, and doing it produced two measurements the project did not have. (1) THE RECENT THREATFOX EXPORT IS A SIGHTING WINDOW, NOT A LISTING: all 4 095 entries in the committed snapshot had their last activity between 2026-08-31 and 2026-09-02, a two-day span, and 3 104 of them were first seen before that window and are present only because they were seen again. So a corpus must be captured AND enriched contemporaneously; nothing here archives past exports, so retroactive enrichment of an archived capture is impossible rather than merely stale. (2) THE CEILING IS REAL AND NEAR: at the 8 live queries an analyst run may spend and the 4/minute the tool layer holds itself to, one measured network day (12 089 contexts) costs 968 live queries and 4.0 hours of pure rate-limited waiting at 1 % escalation, and 9 672 queries over 40.3 hours at 10 % — 1.68 days of even our own 5 760/day ceiling, and 19.3 days of a published 500/day quota. The experiment that removes the retrieval confound is the one the quota binds hardest.
makes_buildable: The deferred evaluation harness has a specification to be built against instead of guesses: what a label is keyed on, what vocabulary it uses, what it must be able to tell apart, where it is stored (the single store, not a file beside it), and what a run of it may cost in live queries. Task 55's deferred register and open-question closure can cite this file for the corpus item and its eight dependents rather than restating them. Any future retrieval experiment has the design constraint already computed: one live retrieval pass, every other arm replayed through `helena.tools`' replay mode, because k arms retrieving live cost k times the table and stop being contemporaneous.

verification.detail: 1894 passed, 1 skipped in 964.75 s (the skip is tests/test_analyst.py:1725, the live model endpoint returning a typed `timed_out` failure — pre-existing and unrelated). 36 of those tests are the new module: the sizing arithmetic executed against the real config/policy.toml, the snapshot reader against the committed ThreatFox export fixture and against a crafted two-record-under-one-id export, `scripts/corpus_sizing.py` run in a subprocess three ways (no --daily-quota, self-imposed, an unreadable quota), and the document's two ceiling tables and its corpus-size numbers recomputed cell by cell. No SQL was added, so nothing new ran against the engine; the module needs neither engine nor broker and completes in 1.6 s on its own.

deferred: The evaluation harness itself, as the task asks — nothing here reads a label, scores a verdict or compares an arm, and `test_the_harness_is_still_deferred` fails if a module named for one appears inside `helena/`, if `concept/01` stops deferring it, or if the document stops saying so.

Measuring the base rate. It cannot be measured with the artifacts in this repository and that is recorded rather than approximated: the one multi-host capture is 2025-09-20 and the one feed snapshot covers 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-02, so an overlap computed between them would be an artefact of the year between them. Running the join anyway would have produced a plausible number with nothing behind it.

Measuring the corpus's distinct-indicator count, which is the cache's bound on the quota and the lower of the two. `envelope(distinct_indicators=...)` takes it and the report prints it when given; the measured day's 2 490 distinct names are the only part of it this repository has counted (addresses and URLs are not counted anywhere).
An ADR. The reasoning is in the document and `docs/acceptance.md` (task 52) set the precedent of an artifact without one; task 55 owns the decision-record sweep and can decide otherwise.
lessons: task 54: THE 'RECENT' THREATFOX EXPORT IS A ~2-DAY SIGHTING WINDOW, NOT THE PUBLISHER'S LISTING. Measured 2026-09-12 over the committed snapshot: all 4 095 entries' last activity falls between 2026-08-31 and 2026-09-02, and 3 104 of them were FIRST seen before that window — 633 ip:port entries more than 183 days before it, one as far back as 2021 — so they are in the export because they were seen again. Two consequences: reading `first_seen_utc` to date a snapshot reports a five-year window for a two-day one, and an indicator that is quiet is on neither the export nor the API. `scripts/corpus_sizing.py --snapshot` re-derives it.

task 54: THE LIVE-QUERY CEILING ON ANY EVALUATION IS 720 ANALYST RUNS A DAY, and it is arithmetic rather than an opinion: 8 live queries per analyst run (derived by `helena.budgets.load` from 120 retrieval seconds and 4 queries/minute) against the 5 760/day our own rate limit implies. One measured network day at 10 % escalation is 1.68 days of that. A published 500/day quota — VirusTotal's, the independent second source — brings it to 62 runs a day, so the experiment that would remove the retrieval confound is the one the quota binds hardest.

task 54: A DOCUMENT'S NUMBERS ARE A DUPLICATED CONSTANT, and the version-constant rule applies to them. `tests/test_evaluation_corpus.py` parses the two ceiling tables out of `docs/evaluation-corpus.md` and recomputes every cell from `config/policy.toml`, so moving `retrieval_seconds` or a rate limit fails the document rather than leaving it quietly describing a system that no longer exists. Same shape as `tests/test_end_to_end.py` parsing `concept/01`'s claims and `tests/test_conformance.py` parsing the must-never-happen table — three documents now, one mechanism.

task 54: CORPUS SIZE IS SET BY POSITIVES, NOT BY CONTEXTS. 62 labelled positives buy a 95 % interval of ±10 % on a rate near 0.8 and 246 buy ±5 % (halving the width quadruples the labelling). At a 0.1 % base rate that first number is 62 000 contexts — about five days of the measured network — so 'is the corpus big enough' is unanswerable until somebody has measured how often anything is there at all, and the honest form of the requirement is conditional.

task 54: SEVERAL RESEARCH QUESTIONS ARE NOT BLOCKED BY THE CORPUS FIRST. RQ7 (cloud investigation) and RQ8 (cross-context memory) are blocked by a missing component before a missing label; RQ6 (replay) needs a population of real runs rather than labels at all; and half of RQ5 is already structurally guaranteed by MNH-04 rather than pending measurement. Only four of the eight are blocked squarely on labels. 'Everything is blocked on the corpus' was the summary, and it was too coarse to plan against.
failed_approaches: task 54: Measuring the base rate by joining the demo day's contexts against the committed ThreatFox snapshot. Started, then rejected before running it: the traffic is 2025-09-20 and the snapshot's whole activity window is 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-02, so any hit rate between them measures the year of drift and not a base rate — and it would have been the first number in the document with nothing behind it. The finding IS that the measurement is blocked; §6 says so and the deferred list records it.

task 54: Putting the sizing arithmetic in a module under `src/helena/`. `tests/test_package_layout.py` requires one module per architecture component with a justification comment in the test, and an evaluation instrument is not a component of the pipeline; it is also the shape that would make 'the harness is deferred' quietly untrue. `scripts/measure_rendering.py` is the precedent — an instrument in `scripts/`, maturity-labelled, cited by the document whose number it produced — and `tests/conftest.py` already puts `scripts/` on the path, so it is tested like anything else.

task 54: Having `snapshot_window` read every `*.json` in a directory as a bulk export. `tests/fixtures/threatfox/` holds the hunting API's responses beside the export and they are a different shape, so the reader crashed on a string index. It now refuses a file that is not an export and names it — accepting both would have reported a plausible window over a handful of hand-picked indicators, which is exactly the confound the document is about.
next_session_should_know: Task 55 (governance: decision records, the deferred register, open-question closure) is the immediate consumer. Three things to carry into it. (1) `docs/evaluation-corpus.md` §9 already holds a deferred table and a twelve-item acceptance checklist for a corpus; the register should cite it rather than restate it, and `tests/test_evaluation_corpus.py::test_the_harness_is_still_deferred` is the executable half. (2) There is a wording discrepancy worth resolving there rather than here: `docs/decisions/0028-the-threatfox-hunting-api.md` §7 says the publisher 'expires IOCs older than six months', which reads as first-seen and is not what the export shows — 633 ip:port entries first seen more than 183 days before the snapshot are in it, all with activity inside its two-day window. The sentence is right if 'older' means 'last seen', and the measurement in `docs/evaluation-corpus.md` §4 is the evidence either way. (3) This task deliberately wrote no ADR; if the governance sweep decides a research artifact needs one, the reasoning is already in the document and would only need a record pointing at it. Also worth knowing generally: the full suite is now 1 894 tests in ~965 s on this machine (877 in ~376 s at task 26, 963 in ~480 s at task 28) — budget a session against sixteen minutes, and run it in the foreground, because a session's turn ending is the session ending.
